title: Commission Clawback on a Deal Closed Before the Window Shortened
scenario_text:
Rainier Software administers sales commissions and clawbacks under its Incentive Compensation Policy.

Policy v1 (in effect through 2024-12-31): "If a customer churns within 6 months of the deal-close date, 100% of the commission paid on that deal is clawed back. No proration applies."

Policy v2 (effective 2025-01-01): "If a customer churns within 4 months of the deal-close date, 50% of the commission paid is clawed back." v2 adds a transition clause: "Commissions on deals closed before January 1, 2025 remain subject to the v1 clawback terms (6-month window, 100%, no proration). Deals closed on or after January 1, 2025 follow v2. The deal-close date is the contract signature date, not the invoice or payment date."

The commissions ledger shows deal D-4410 (rep: T. Okafor, customer: Summit Freight): Contract Signature Date 2024-11-15, Invoice Date 2024-12-05, Commission Paid $40,000. The churn management system records that Summit Freight gave notice and fully terminated on 2025-03-10, citing a budget freeze rather than any service failure. The rep's payout on D-4410 was disbursed in the December 2024 commission run, and no retention exception or credit was logged against the account.

A compensation analyst emails the RevOps controller on 2025-03-12: "Processing the Summit Freight clawback. The deal signed in November 2024, but the churn happened in March 2025, which is only about four months out. Under the new rule that's a 50% clawback, but the deal is old. How much do we claw back from Okafor?"

Using the policy history, the transition clause, and the ledger, determine the clawback amount on D-4410.
question: What is the clawback amount on deal D-4410?
